docs.text: BagaCAD Draw lines, circles and rectangles, offset edges, extrude and edit dimensions directly in Blender. 0.22 Alpha · Blender 5.0+ Install Drag the BagaCAD extension ZIP from your file browser into Blender, then confirm installation. Keep the ZIP intact; enable BagaCAD if prompted. Disable older development copies first. You can also use Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions > menu > Install from Disk… . Both methods are described in the Blender manual . Start Open the 3D Viewport sidebar with N , then select BagaCAD . Key or gesture Action Click Draw in the panel Draw on the active mesh; create an empty mesh if no mesh is active C / B / O during Draw Circle / rectangle / offset; also available as panel buttons Click Dimensions in the panel Start directly in dimension editing on the active mesh F3 > BagaCAD New Drawing Create an empty mesh and start drawing F3 > BagaCAD Draw Start drawing on the active mesh Click Documentation in the panel Open this manual Click points to draw. Close a flat contour to make a face. The viewport header shows the current action. The Dimensions button needs an active mesh. Draw · Shapes & offsets · Guides & grid · Extrude · Dimensions · Shortcuts & settings Short GIF demonstrations are included in the tool pages. Some recordings use earlier development builds; the written shortcuts describe the current defaults. Scope BagaCAD edits the active mesh. Other objects can hide snap targets but are not themselves snap targets. Hidden mesh elements are ignored. X-Ray and Wireframe allow snapping to revealed geometry. Non-planar contours stay open. Dimensions and their locks are temporary tool data, not a persistent CAD constraint system. This alpha is still in development.

docs.text: Dimensions Click Dimensions in N > BagaCAD , or press D while drawing, then select a vertex or an edge. Near an endpoint, the vertex takes priority. A single selected or active element may be picked automatically. A selected vertex shows its incident edge lengths and useful angles. A selected edge shows its length, nearby parallel distances and angles. Lengths follow the scene units; angles use degrees. Change a value Edit the dimensions around a selected vertex; connected faces follow. Key or gesture Action Click a vertex or edge Select the element to measure and edit Click a value Highlight it in blue and type a replacement Drag a value left / right Decrease / increase it Release the drag Confirm the change Ctrl while dragging Use the configured length or angle increments Shift while dragging Adjust ten times more finely Enter / click during input Confirm typed input Esc / right click during input Cancel the edit Ctrl + A during input Select the whole value Ctrl + V during input Paste a value Backspace during input Delete a character Lengths accept units such as mm , cm , m , ft and in . Angles accept values from −360° to 360°. Typed values do not use drag rounding. Vertex anchoring A selected vertex starts anchored . Click its support icon or press Tab outside input to toggle anchoring. Anchored: the selected vertex stays fixed; its neighbours adapt. Free: only the selected vertex moves; the opposite endpoints remain fixed. Shared faces follow without detaching. With no other length locked, a length edit moves along that edge. With locked lengths, the vertex can change direction while free angles adapt. The solver chooses the nearest position satisfying those lengths. For example, at a three-edge corner, lock two lengths and edit the third if a geometric solution exists. If the locks conflict, the edit is refused and the preview restored. Readable angles The display hides composite angles already described by smaller coplanar sectors and redundant directions. Equal angles in different useful sectors can remain; a cube corner keeps its three independent right angles. Locked and currently edited angles remain visible. Arc sizes follow the visible edges and zoom. Labels sit near their arcs with staggered radii to reduce overlap. This changes the display, not the stored constraints. Edge fixed end and locks Key or gesture Action Tab outside input / click the support icon Switch the fixed endpoint of the selected edge Hover a value Reveal its padlock Click the padlock Lock / unlock that dimension A length edit moves the free endpoint along the edge. A parallel distance edit translates the edge. Angle edits try to slide connected endpoints along neighboring directions, changing the edited length when needed to limit distortion. Locked values are kept while neighboring geometry adjusts. If constraints conflict, cancel or unlock a value. Locks last only while Dimensions is active; leaving the mode clears them. Undo and return Key or gesture Action Ctrl + Z during input or a drag Cancel the current preview Ctrl + Z outside input Undo a validated change Backspace outside input Deselect the element Backspace during a drag Cancel the preview Right click outside input Deselect the element D / Esc outside input Return to drawing

docs.text: Draw Place a start point, then add segments. On a face, hold Ctrl when clicking to draw instead of extruding; keep away from a guide handle. Key or gesture Action Left click Place the start point or confirm the next segment Right click Start a new chain Ctrl + click inside a face Start drawing on the face X / Y / Z Lock the corresponding axis; press again to release Shift + X / Y / Z Lock to YZ / XZ / XY; press again to release Type digits Set the active length or angle value Tab Switch between length and angle input Click / Enter Confirm the segment Backspace Delete a digit; outside input, cancel the unfinished chain Ctrl, held Disable mesh, grid and guide snapping; release to restore snapping Ctrl + Z Undo a validated edit; discard any unfinished guide/grid setup first Esc Clear input, setup or selection; otherwise finish the tool Enter without input or selection Finish the tool Precision Use the coloured axes to align successive segments. A typed length fixes distance while the direction follows the mouse. A typed angle fixes the angle while the length changes. Enter both to fix both. Tab alone selects a field without locking it. Drawing snapping is on by default. Hold Ctrl to disable it; release Ctrl to restore it. Explicit axis/plane locks and typed dimensions stay active without Ctrl. Hovering can still acquire construction guides and temporary references. Snap targets include vertices, midpoints, edges, faces, construction guides and grid nodes. With a fixed length, any snap target can choose the direction; the segment keeps its entered length. Displayed measurements follow the scene units. Drawing input uses Blender units; angles use degrees. In empty space without a snap, grid plane or explicit constraint, the first point uses a view-parallel plane through the 3D cursor. Each following segment uses a view-parallel plane through its starting point instead. For circles, rectangles and parallel edges, see Shapes & offsets . Faces Close the contour to create a face. Close a flat contour to fill it. Draw between face borders to cut a face. Crossings split edges; overlapping segments merge. To fill a missing flat region, retrace one of its border edges. Existing coplanar faces are not covered. A diagonal across an empty square can fill both sides. Erase and extend edges Key or gesture Action Hold Shift + right mouse, then sweep Erase visible edges under the cursor Release right mouse or Shift End the stroke; one undo step for the whole sweep Esc / Ctrl + Z during the stroke Cancel the sweep and restore the mesh Hold Alt over an edge Preview extension from the endpoint nearest the cursor Alt + left click on the preview Extend to the first real vertex, edge or face target Release Alt Hide the extension preview Erasing B–C in A–B–C–D keeps A–B and C–D. A divider between coplanar faces is dissolved while preserving the surface. Erasing a boundary or an edge between non-coplanar faces also removes its attached faces. Extension joins the target in 3D; a screen-only crossing is not enough. Inside a face plane it targets real boundaries; a transverse arrival into a face makes a local cut. Without a visible target, clicking does nothing. Alt priority: a hovered guide moves first; otherwise an edge can extend, while a face interior keeps coplanar extrusion. In Rectangle, Alt centres the shape. Navigation Key or gesture Action Middle mouse / Shift + middle mouse / wheel Orbit / pan / zoom with the default Blender keymap Numpad during a segment Enter numbers Numpad before the first point Use Blender view shortcuts BagaCAD shortcuts can be changed in the preferences ; navigation uses Blender's keymap.

docs.text: Extrude Hover inside a face with no segment in progress. A light overlay marks the extrusion target. Start the extrusion, move the mouse, then confirm. The face moves along its normal. Key or gesture Action Click a highlighted face Start an extrusion preview Move the mouse Adjust the extrusion distance Type a distance Set an exact distance in Blender units Minus Change the direction of the typed distance Backspace Correct typed distance; without input, cancel the preview Click / Enter during the preview Confirm the extrusion Esc / right click / Ctrl + Z during the preview Cancel it and restore the original mesh Ctrl + Z after confirmation Undo the whole extrusion in one step Undo affects the latest validated edit. Cancelling a preview leaves earlier edits in the local history; press Ctrl + Z again to undo the previous edit. An empty history does nothing. After leaving BagaCAD, Blender handles undo. Extrude the new face into a volume. Several faces Key or gesture Action Shift + click Add / remove a face from the selection Plain click on a selected face Extrude the selection Enter with a selection Extrude along the last selected face's normal Alt + click Replace the selection with connected coplanar faces and extrude them Esc / right click before extrusion Clear the selection For non-coplanar selected faces, the group moves in one common direction: the normal of the last selected face. Coplanar selection spreads only through shared edges, not corner contacts or detached faces. Snapping Height snapping is off by default and is active only while Ctrl is held. Key or gesture Action Hold Ctrl and aim at a vertex, midpoint, edge or face Place the extruded face plane through that snap point Hold Ctrl during extrusion Enable height snapping; release for free movement Orbit / pan / zoom Change the view while keeping the preview active The face still moves only along its extrusion direction. A typed distance takes priority over snapping. Result Push a face inward to remove material from the same mesh. Outward extrusion can fuse with volumes in the same mesh. Inward extrusion can make a pocket or a through-hole. The exact boolean calculation happens when you confirm and remains one undo step. An isolated surface keeps a bottom and becomes a volume. Other objects remain separate.

docs.text: Guides & grid What is a construction guide? A construction guide is a drawing reference used to position or align geometry. It is not an edge or face in the mesh and is not rendered. In BagaCAD, construction guides include XYZ references, infinite edge lines and the construction grid. An XYZ reference has one origin and three perpendicular axes. An edge guide extends an edge direction infinitely in both directions. A grid provides evenly spaced snap points on a plane. They complement the mesh snaps instead of replacing them. Guides and temporary references also remain available during circles, rectangles and offsets . The soft plane indicator around the shape cursor does not add snap points. Guides stay available between segments during the active tool session. They are not saved as scene objects. The grid has its own show/hide command and remembers its last setup for that session. Key or gesture Action Hover a vertex or edge midpoint for 2 s Add an XYZ construction guide Hover an edge away from its midpoint and ends for 2 s Add an infinite guide along that edge A on a vertex, then click another vertex Add a guide through both vertices Hold Alt over a guide, then move Move the guide; release to confirm Hold Shift over an XYZ axis, then aim Rotate the whole XYZ reference around its fixed origin; release to confirm X / Y / Z while holding Shift to rotate XYZ Lock rotation around that initial local guide axis; repeat to unlock Esc / right click during a transformation Cancel the preview R Remove the last XYZ or edge guide Shift + R Clear XYZ/edge guides and temporary references; the grid is unchanged Moving an XYZ reference moves its three axes together. An edge guide keeps its direction and can snap through a chosen point. Guide intersections must meet in 3D; a crossing visible only on screen is not a snap. Use an edge extension as a guide for a new contour. This clip uses an earlier development build; use the shortcuts listed above. What is a temporary reference point? A temporary reference point remembers a position briefly to help align the next segment. It does not create permanent construction geometry. Its projections offer XYZ directions and the extensions of edges meeting at that point. Dotted links show which reference supplies the snap. Key or gesture Action Hover a vertex for 0.15 s, then move away Remember it and use its temporary projections Hover a guide/guide or guide/edge intersection for 0.15 s Remember that intersection as a temporary reference Acquire a third temporary point Replace the oldest of the two remembered points Confirm a segment / start a new chain / clear guides Clear the temporary references Two temporary points can work together, including intersections with construction guides. Following a temporary axis can also snap to its intersection with a plane through the other point: XY, YZ, XZ or an incident face plane. Those planes stay invisible; a violet dotted link identifies the relation. A short hover acquires a temporary reference; continuing the hover can create a construction guide where supported. The four hover delays are editable in preferences . Construction grid Key or gesture Action G Show / hide the remembered grid; on first use, create XY at the 3D cursor Shift + G Place or reorient the grid in two clicks: origin, then X direction G while choosing the second direction point Toggle using the measured segment length as cell size Hold Ctrl at the second direction click Use that segment length as cell size Ctrl + G Set cell size by measuring a segment or typing a number, then Enter Alt + G Place and align the grid to the hovered face Shift + X / Y / Z, no segment active Orient a world grid to YZ / XZ / XY Esc / right click during setup Cancel setup and restore the previous grid G normally hides the grid; during direction setup it controls the cell-size option instead. Hiding and showing it preserves its origin, orientation and cell size. R and Shift + R do not hide it. The grid snaps only to line intersections, not cell centers or side midpoints. Its default step is 0.1 Blender unit. Mesh, guide and temporary-reference snaps remain available with the grid active. While drawing, snapping to these references and grid nodes is enabled by default. Hold Ctrl to disable snapping; the grid remains a drawing plane without rounding to nodes. Grid setup and guide editing keep their own point picking. During an XYZ rotation, X/Y/Z refer to the guide frame at the start of the gesture, including tilted guides. The origin and the selected rotation axis stay fixed; all three axes rotate together. If the grabbed axis is itself the rotation axis, the next local axis supplies the aiming direction. A target on the rotation axis leaves the last valid orientation unchanged. Hold Alt over any XYZ, edge or custom construction guide to move it. Snapping is active immediately; release Alt to confirm, or use Esc / right click / Backspace to cancel. Over a guide, this takes priority over coplanar-face selection. Away from guides, Alt keeps its face-selection behavior.

docs.text: Shapes & offsets Use C , B or O during Draw, or the matching button in N > BagaCAD . Press the active tool key again to return to lines. Esc / right click cancels the current shape and returns to Draw. Each confirmed shape is one undo step. Circles and arcs Key or gesture Action C, then two clicks Circle: centre, then radius Type a radius after placing the centre Set an exact radius; click / Enter to confirm Tab Switch centre-radius / three-point method; restart the current shape Three clicks in three-point mode Create a full circle through the three points V Switch full circle / open arc, keeping placed points Wheel after the first click Change segment count without zooming For a centre-based arc, click the centre , start/radius , then end ; the arc runs counterclockwise in its drawing plane. For a three-point arc, it runs from the first point to the third through the second. The radius and edge count appear on the preview. The initial resolution is 48 segments , configurable in preferences; the wheel allows 3–256 during drawing. Before the first click, the wheel still zooms. Arcs remain open lines. Rectangles and squares Key or gesture Action B, then two clicks First corner, then opposite corner Hold Shift Constrain to a square Hold Alt First point becomes the centre; aim at a corner Hold Shift + Alt Centred square Type a size, then Tab Enter width, then height; Tab switches the active side Both side lengths appear on the preview. The active value is highlighted beside its side; the first digit after Tab replaces the previous value. For centred shapes, width and height are the total dimensions . Drawing plane and references Before each new circle or rectangle, hover the target face. Its plane is detected before the first click, including from an incident face when snapping to an edge or vertex. Without a face, the tool uses the active grid, then guides or the view. The plane stays fixed after the first click and is detected again for the next shape. The soft grid around the cursor shows this plane; it is an indicator, not an extra snap grid. X / Y / Z after the first point orients the shape plane to YZ / XZ / XY in the current reference frame. A three-point circle uses the actual 3D snapped points to determine its plane. Hover references and construction guides remain available while drawing shapes and offsets. A creates a two-point guide; G and grid setup commands stay available. Hold Ctrl to suspend placement snapping. The snap marker stays on the target even when the shape needs a projection onto its plane. Offset edges Press O , click an edge, move to the desired side, then click to confirm. Type a distance for an exact offset; the mouse chooses the side. For several edges: O → hold Shift → click the edges → release Shift → move/type → click . Each click adds only the targeted edge, shown in orange. Releasing Shift groups the selection into chains and starts the preview from the last selected edge. Independent chains share the distance and one undo step. Source edges remain in place. Chains must be planar; corners use miter joins and self-crossing offsets are rejected. Offsets work on existing faces or loose edges. Filled faces or lines only Closed shapes create faces by default. Hold F to invert filling while placing a circle, rectangle or offset. The preference Shapes: Create Faces by Default reverses this default. With filling enabled, an offset also creates the connecting strip. With filling disabled, it creates only parallel lines. On an existing face, the new lines still cut the surface: disabling fill does not remove existing material. Shared edges and intersections merge into the active mesh.
docs.title: Shapes & offsets

docs.text: Use C , B or O during Draw, or the matching button in N > BagaCAD . Press the active tool key again to return to lines. Esc / right click cancels the current shape and returns to Draw. Each confirmed shape is one undo step.

docs.text: Key or gesture Action C, then two clicks Circle: centre, then radius Type a radius after placing the centre Set an exact radius; click / Enter to confirm Tab Switch centre-radius / three-point method; restart the current shape Three clicks in three-point mode Create a full circle through the three points V Switch full circle / open arc, keeping placed points Wheel after the first click Change segment count without zooming For a centre-based arc, click the centre , start/radius , then end ; the arc runs counterclockwise in its drawing plane. For a three-point arc, it runs from the first point to the third through the second. The radius and edge count appear on the preview. The initial resolution is 48 segments , configurable in preferences; the wheel allows 3–256 during drawing. Before the first click, the wheel still zooms. Arcs remain open lines.
docs.title: Circles and arcs

docs.text: Key or gesture Action B, then two clicks First corner, then opposite corner Hold Shift Constrain to a square Hold Alt First point becomes the centre; aim at a corner Hold Shift + Alt Centred square Type a size, then Tab Enter width, then height; Tab switches the active side Both side lengths appear on the preview. The active value is highlighted beside its side; the first digit after Tab replaces the previous value. For centred shapes, width and height are the total dimensions .
docs.title: Rectangles and squares

docs.text: Before each new circle or rectangle, hover the target face. Its plane is detected before the first click, including from an incident face when snapping to an edge or vertex. Without a face, the tool uses the active grid, then guides or the view. The plane stays fixed after the first click and is detected again for the next shape. The soft grid around the cursor shows this plane; it is an indicator, not an extra snap grid. X / Y / Z after the first point orients the shape plane to YZ / XZ / XY in the current reference frame. A three-point circle uses the actual 3D snapped points to determine its plane. Hover references and construction guides remain available while drawing shapes and offsets. A creates a two-point guide; G and grid setup commands stay available. Hold Ctrl to suspend placement snapping. The snap marker stays on the target even when the shape needs a projection onto its plane.
docs.title: Drawing plane and references

docs.text: Press O , click an edge, move to the desired side, then click to confirm. Type a distance for an exact offset; the mouse chooses the side. For several edges: O → hold Shift → click the edges → release Shift → move/type → click . Each click adds only the targeted edge, shown in orange. Releasing Shift groups the selection into chains and starts the preview from the last selected edge. Independent chains share the distance and one undo step. Source edges remain in place. Chains must be planar; corners use miter joins and self-crossing offsets are rejected. Offsets work on existing faces or loose edges.
docs.title: Offset edges

docs.text: Closed shapes create faces by default. Hold F to invert filling while placing a circle, rectangle or offset. The preference Shapes: Create Faces by Default reverses this default. With filling enabled, an offset also creates the connecting strip. With filling disabled, it creates only parallel lines. On an existing face, the new lines still cut the surface: disabling fill does not remove existing material. Shared edges and intersections merge into the active mesh.
docs.title: Filled faces or lines only

docs.text: Shortcuts & settings The tables show the default bindings . Customize them in Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > BagaCAD . The header and sidebar reminders follow your settings. Construction references Key or gesture Action Hover a vertex / midpoint for 2 s Add an XYZ guide Hover an edge interior for 2 s Add an edge guide Hover a vertex / guide intersection for 0.15 s Acquire a temporary reference point A on a vertex, then click another Add a guide through the two vertices Hold Alt over a guide Move it Hold Shift over an XYZ axis Rotate that reference X / Y / Z during rotation Lock the local rotation axis; repeat to unlock R / Shift + R Remove last guide / clear guides and temporary points; preserve grid G Show / hide the grid Shift + G Reposition / reorient the grid Ctrl + G Set cell size Alt + G Align grid to a face G during direction setup / Ctrl at second click Use direction-segment length as cell size Dimensions Key or gesture Action Click / drag a value Type / adjust it Ctrl while dragging Use rounding increments Shift while dragging Use fine adjustment Tab outside input / click support icon Edge: switch fixed endpoint; vertex: toggle anchoring Hover a value, then click its padlock Toggle the dimension lock Ctrl + A / Ctrl + V during input Select all / paste D / Esc outside input Return to Draw Preferences Setting Default Create Guide Timer 2.0 s Edge Guide Delay 2.0 s Temporary Vertex Delay 0.15 s Temporary Intersection Delay 0.15 s Grid Step 0.1 Blender unit Shapes: Create Faces by Default Enabled; F temporarily inverts it Circle Segments 48 (preference: 8–256; wheel while drawing: 3–256) Length Snap Step 10 cm Angle Snap Step 15° The length and angle increments apply only to Ctrl-dragging dimensions. Display Text controls labels near the cursor. Shortcut rows configure keys and modifiers. Shared input keys configure picking, confirmation, cancellation and text correction. Hold modifiers configure related gestures together; use a different modifier for each row. Red rows flag conflicting bindings. Right-click a setting to reset it to its default. Saved preferences can differ from these defaults. Digits, decimal separators and minus remain numeric input. View navigation follows Blender's own keymap. The viewport header changes with the current step: start point, segment input, face selection, extrusion, guide edit, grid setup or dimension edit. It displays the configured bindings. Ctrl disables drawing snaps but enables extrusion snaps while held; Alt moves a hovered guide.
